title: Protocol to dissociate, process, and analyze the human lung tissue using single-cell RNA-seq
protocol: Place a surgical specimen in a tube filled with 5–20 mL of 1× PBS and place on ice.
Ensure the biospecimen is completely submerged in the PBS solution.
Prepare an enzyme mix comprising 250 μL of Enzyme H, 110 μL of Enzyme R, and 40 μL of Enzyme A provided in the Human Tumor Dissociation Kit (Miltenyi Biotec).
Transfer the prepared enzyme mix into a gentleMACS C-Tube supplemented with 7.5 mL of serum-free cell culture medium.
Aspirate the buffer surrounding the biospecimen.
Transfer the tissue to a 15 mm Petri dish.
Hold the specimen with tweezers and cut it into approximately 5 mm³ pieces using a sharp razor.
Transfer the tissue pieces to a gentleMACS C Tube containing the enzyme mix prepared at step #3.
Place the gentleMACS C-Tube in the gentleMACS Octo Dissociator with Heaters.
Run the default program “37C_H_TDK3” for 15 minutes.
Inspect the quality of dissociation by eye.
Proceed to the next step if no tissue chunks are visible, otherwise run the program for an additional 10 minutes.
Pass the dissociated cells through a 70 μm cell strainer placed in a 50 mL conical tube.
Rinse the 70 μm cell strainer with 20-25 mL of Cell Resuspension buffer.
Split the flow-through suspension into two 15 mL tubes.
Spin at 800 × g for 3 min at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully without disturbing the cell pellet, leaving ∼50-100 μL on top of the pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1-2 mL of Red Blood Cell Lysis Solution (ACK buffer) by slowly pipetting up and down 2-3 times.
Incubate for 2 min at 20°C–25°C.
Dilute ACK buffer by adding 20 mL of Cell Resuspension buffer.
Split the suspension into two 15 mL tubes.
Centrifuge at 800 × g at 20°C–25°C for 3 min.
Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 3-4 mL of refrigerated Cell Resuspension buffer.
Transfer onto a 35 μm Cell Strainer Snap Cap and let the fluid pass through by gravity.
Use Human Tumor Dissociation Kit to prepare an enzyme mix comprising 85 μL of Enzyme H, 40 μL of Enzyme R, and 15 μL of Enzyme A.
Transfer the enzyme mix into a gentleMACS C-Tube supplemented with 2.5 mL of serum-free cell culture medium (e.g., RPMI-1640).
Centrifuge the tube containing the core biopsy piece(s) at 800 × g for 2 min at 20°C–25°C.
Discard the supernatant and transfer the tissue pieces to the GentleMACS C-Tube containing the enzyme mix.
Place the GentleMACS C-Tube in the GentleMACS Octo Dissociator with Heaters, and run default program “37C_H_TDK3” for 15 min.
Verify the dissociation by visually inspecting the solution.
If tissue is not completely dissociated, continue running the program for additional 5 min.
Add 7.5 mM sterile NaOH to achieve a stock concentration of 1.25 mg/ml for leptin.
Rinse the GentleMACS C Tube with 1.5 mL of Cell Resuspension Buffer and transfer the suspension onto the same Cell Strainer Snap Cap.
Collect any left-over cells from the rinse into the Test Tube containing the cell suspension.
Spin the Test Tube at 800 × g for 2 minutes at a temperature between 20°C–25°C.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant using a glass Pasteur pipette coupled to a vacuum source, leaving ∼30-50 μL of supernatant on top of the cell pellet.
Add 200 μL of Red Blood Cell Lysis Solution (ACK buffer) to the cell pellet and gently resuspend by slowly pipetting up and down 2-3 times.
Incubate for 2 minutes at a temperature between 20°C–25°C.
Dilute the ACK buffer with 2 mL of Cell Resuspension Buffer after incubation.
Centrifuge the diluted solution at 800 × g for 2 minutes at a temperature between 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet, leaving ∼30 μL of supernatant on top of the cell pellet.
Transfer pleural effusion fluid into conical 50 mL tubes.
Centrifuge at 500 × g at 20°C–25°C for 10 min.
Carefully remove the supernatant, leaving ∼50 μL of supernatant on top of the cell pellet.
Disperse the cell pellet in the remaining supernatant.
Repeat the process for each tube.
Combine all cell suspensions in 15–20 mL of Cell Resuspension buffer.
Load approximately 15 mL of Ficoll-Paque PLUS into the SepMate-50 (IVD) tube until the fluid level is just above the dividing plastic.
Layer 20 mL of concentrated cell suspension onto the Ficoll-Paque PLUS in the SepMate-50 (IVD) tube without mixing.
Centrifuge the SepMate-50 (IVD) tube at 1,200 × g for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C with the centrifuge accelerator and brake turned off.
Remove 15 mL of upper fluid layer from each SepMate-50 (IVD) tube into a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Gently pipette up and down to disperse and collect the residue above the dividing plastic in the remaining ∼5 mL solution.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 3 minutes at 20°C–25°C and discard the supernatant, leaving approximately 50 μL on top of the cell pellet.
Add 200 μL of Red Blood Cell Lysis Solution (ACK buffer) to a cell pellet and gently resuspend by pipetting up and down 2-3 times.
Incubate for 2 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Dilute ACK buffer by adding 2 mL of Cell Resuspension buffer.
Centrifuge the diluted ACK buffer at 800 × g for 2 min at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet, leaving ∼30 μL on top of the cell pellet.
Proceed to “Part D. Cell staining with live-dye and anti-CD45 antibody” section if necessary.
Centrifuge the cells in FACS tube at 800 × g for 3 min at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate supernatant carefully without disturbing the cell pellet.
Leave 50 μL of supernatant on top of the cell pellet.
Prepare Cell Staining Mix for live-cells or CD45-negative cells.
Combine 50 μl cell suspension with 100 μl Cell Staining Mix per roughly 10^6 cells.
Gently rock the tube or pipette up and down 2–3 times to disperse the cells.
Incubate on ice for 15 minutes.
Dilute the Cell Staining Mix by adding 2 mL of refrigerated Cell Resuspension Buffer.
Centrifuge in a swinging bucket centrifuge at 800 × g for 3 minutes.
Aspirate supernatant carefully.
Add 2 mL of RPMI-FBS and centrifuge at 800 × g for 3 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellet in ice-cold 100 μL RPMI-FBS.
Add DAPI dye at a final concentration of 0.1–1 μg/mL.
Place the tube on ice.
Prepare 1.5 mL Protein LoBind Eppendorf tubes with 50 μL of RPMI-FBS.
Follow the instructions of the corresponding FACS instrument to initiate the flow cytometry.
Set appropriate sorting gates for capturing the live-cell populations of interest.
Use the side scatter (SSC-A) and forward scatter (FSC-A) plot to discard debris, but be inclusive to avoid potential loss of cells of interest.
Utilize the side scatter height (SSC-H) and side scatter width (SSC-W) plot for gating.
Employ the forward scatter height (FSC-H) and forward scatter width (FSC-W) plot to gate singlets.
Use the DAPI and forward scatter plot to identify live-cells (DAPI negative), but be inclusive due to the complexity of clinical samples.
Prepare FITC (Calcein) and PE (CD45) scatter plot to enrich live cells that are positive for FITC.
Separate immune cells (CD45 positive) from non-immune cells (CD45 negative) in the PE (CD45) channel.
Set sorting gates negative for DAPI and PE to enrich live non-immune (tumor-enriched) cells, and positive for Calcein.
Set sorting gates negative for DAPI and positive for both Calcein and PE to enrich live immune cells.
If tumor cell enrichment is not required and CD45 staining was not performed, set the sorting gate negative for DAPI and positive for Calcein dyes.
Initiate cell sorting and collect FACS-sorted cells into a 1.5 mL Protein LoBind tube filled with 50 μL of RPMI-FBS.
Record the count of CD45neg and CD45pos events during FACS.
If the sorted CD45neg cell count is ≥50,000, proceed to the next step.
If the sorted CD45neg cell count ≤50,000, combine the sorted CD45neg cells with sorted CD45pos cells to obtain at least 50,000 total cells.
Centrifuge the combined cells at 800 × g for 4 min at 4°C.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Gently resuspend the cell pellet in a required volume of RPMI-FBS medium to obtain approximately 1,500 cells/μL.
Mix 5 μL of cell suspension with 5 μL of 0.4% (w/v) Trypan Blue Solution.
Inspect the cells using a hemocytometer under a bright field microscope.
Alternatively, use an automated cell counter to count viable cells.
Perform a quick visual check of the automated cell counter results by inspecting trypan blue stained cells under a bright field microscope.
Refer to troubleshooting table if cell viability is below 60% or cell count is below 500 cells/μL.
Proceed to next step if cell viability is ≥80% and cell count is ≥500 cells/μL.
Adjust the cell loading concentration to reach a desirable target of barcoded-cells as per Methods S1 (page 24).
Follow the manual for Chromium Controller to load the cells onto Chromium Chip B (Methods S1, pages 25–32).
Perform barcoding RT reaction.
Amplify barcoded-cDNA by 12 cycles of PCR.
Dilute 1 μL sample with 5 μL water.
Load 1 μL of diluted sample onto an Agilent Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity chip.
Fragment the PCR-amplified cDNA library.
Ligate sequencing adaptor to the fragmented DNA.
Perform indexing PCR.
Purify the indexed library using SPRI beads (0.6–0.8×).
Determine the DNA concentration of the final library using Qubit 4.0 Fluorometer and dsDNA HS Assay Kit.
Determine the average fragment size of the final DNA library by diluting 1 μL sample with 9 μL water.
Load 1 μL of diluted DNA library on an Agilent Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity chip.
Select the region encompassing 35–10,000 bp and record the DNA concentration.
Denature and dilute the quantified and normalized DNA libraries as recommended for Illumina sequencing platforms.
Pool individual DNA libraries from different clinical samples into one tube before denaturation.
Dilute each DNA library down to a 2 nM concentration using 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.5.
Filter out cells with low library complexity by regressing the number of detected genes per cell against the number of molecules in the same cell.
Exclude cells if their corresponding residual is greater than 3 standard deviations below the mean.
Use CB2 for empty droplet filtering, setting the “lower” parameter at 100 to estimate ambient RNA background distribution.
Apply an FDR threshold of 0.01 for identifying real cells.
Filter doublets using the DoubletDetection package with default parameters.
Alternatively, filter doublets using Scrublet with default settings.
Retain genes expressed in more than 10 cells for further analysis.
Normalize count matrix by library size.
Scale by median library size.
Log2-transform with a pseudocount of 0.1.
Perform batch correction in the combined dataset using fastMNN.
Apply cosine distance to the log2 transform of the library-size normalized count matrix with pseudocount of 1.
Reduce to the top 50 principal components (PCs).
Merge samples from the same patient first, then merge by histology, prioritizing samples with a greater number of cells.
Construct a k-nearest neighbors’ graph (k=30) from the normalized dataset using Euclidean distance.
Compute the fraction of cells qT derived from each tumor sample T in the neighborhood of each cell j.
Calculate the Shannon entropy Hj of sample frequencies within each cell’s neighborhood.
Cluster cells using the Phenograph algorithm based on the top retained principal components over a range of k values.
Choose k from the window where the adjusted Rand index between clusters is consistently highest.
Use k = 30 for stable clustering in all cell compartments except T-cells, where use k = 40.
Down-sample cells to homogenize sampling per batch prior to differential expression analysis.
Partition cells from each cluster into 10 equally-sized bins based on cell complexity.
Subsample from each bin to at most k cells per sample, where k is the median sample size.
Ensure cell complexity distribution is consistent across samples after downsampling.
Use MAST version 1.8.2 to perform differential expression analysis between SCLC subtypes and rest.
Analyze differential expression between SCLC-A and SCLC-N cells using MAST.
Perform differential expression analysis between each unsupervised cluster and the rest using MAST.
Construct the regression model based on cellular detection rate, tissue status, and treatment status.
Include condition, tissue type, treatment status, and cngeneson in the model.
Transform gene expression levels by natural logarithm with a pseudocount of 1.
Filter differentially expressed genes (DEGs) for significance based on Bonferroni-adjusted p-value < 0.05.
Exclude DEGs with absolute log fold-change < 0.3.
Identify and remove candidate DEGs that could represent ambient RNA using a stepwise regression-based approach.
Fit an initial Loess regression on gene expression for each general cell type versus all other cells.
Bin genes by expression into 25 bins.
Consider the 50 genes with the most negative residuals per bin.
Fit a second linear regression to genes with the most negative residuals.
Exclude genes with residuals for the second regression that are < 2 as ambient RNA.
Calculate gene ranks using -log(p-value)∗log fold change based on MAST differential expression.
Input gene ranks into pre-ranked GSEA using the R package fGSEA.
Use 10,000 permutations for the analysis.
Base pathways on MSigDB v 7.1 curated set from Chan et al., Cancer Cell, 2021.
Consider pathways with Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values < 0.1 to be significant.
Perform non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) using scikit-learn.
Set tolerance for stopping condition at 10−4 and maximum number of iterations at 500.
Calculate reconstruction error for each NMF over a range of k from 5 to 100.
Select the final value of k based on the kneepoint of the log2 reconstruction error.
Ensure robustness to value of k based on Pearson’s correlation between cell loadings.
Set k = 30 for optimal robust factorization.
Annotate factors by genes with the highest loadings.
Scale gene loadings by standard deviation across genes.
Z-score gene expression data across factors.
Extract top features for each factor using ExtractTopFeatures function from CountClust package.
Perform partition-based graph abstraction (PAGA) using Phenograph clusters.
Plot UMAP projections using knn = 15, min_dist = 0.3–0.5, and init_pos = ‘paga’.
Impute gene expression data using MAGIC with knn = 30 and t=3.
Identify cell types based on predominant expression of key gene markers.
Coarse cell typing: Identify immune cells based on PTPRC expression.
Z-score the expression matrix.
Use the score_genes function in scanpy, which calculates the average expression of each cell type-specific gene set and subtracts from the average expression of a reference set of genes.
Smooth cell type labels by choosing the most frequent cell type label per cluster.
Exclude any clusters containing cells derived from normal adjacent lung samples.
Leverage single nucleotide variants (SNVs) identified in clinical DNA sequencing of a targeted panel of 468 genes performed on matched bulk tumors using the MSK IMPACT platform.
Obtain variant calls, including base changes and genomic coordinates, from matched bulk DNA-sequencing.
Identify UMIs from the aligned scRNA-seq bam file that match the same variant calls from bulk DNA-sequencing.
Tally the proportion of UMIs calling SNVs in each epithelial cluster.
Tally the proportion of UMIs calling SNVs in normal immune and mesenchymal cells to serve as a negative control.
Calculate Fisher’s p-value as a measure of enrichment for UMIs that call SNVs.
Adjust the Fisher’s p-value by Bonferroni calculation for multiplicity with a significance threshold of < 0.05.
Leverage copy number variants (CNVs).
Use InferCNV with the following parameters:
Set sliding window of 200 genes.
Base diploid mean and standard deviation on available normal adjacent tumor samples.
Consider CNVs at least two standard deviations from diploid mean.
Calculate CNV burden using fraction of genome affected by CNV.
Calculate CNV burden using Pearson’s correlation between single-cell and bulk CNV profiles.
Compare CNV burden between tumor and normal samples.
Identify cancer cells with a threshold of >10% fraction of genome altered.
Identify cancer cells with Pearson’s correlation to bulk CNV profile rho > 0.2.
Assign the most likely SCLC subtype based on the highest probability.
